order.intro: Your list is ordered by three rules, applied in turn. Here is each rule and what it did today.

rules.title: Causes before the things they cause
rules.body: When one habit sets up another, working on the first often fixes the second for free. We only put one behind another when your swings show it: the second goes away on the swings where the first does.
rules.today: It could not be tested today. All five showed on every swing (or all but one), so there is no swing without one to compare against.

rules.title: Then the biggest miss first

rules.today: This is what set today's order. The bars below show how far each one missed.

workOns.name: Trail knee straightens
workOns.goal: Keep the flex in your trail knee
workOns.saw: Your trail leg straightens going back — on all 10 swings, steady from first swing to last. Typical trail-knee bend lost by the top: 22°, against a target of less than 12°.
workOns.why: A straight trail leg lets your hips slide instead of turn, so you lose power.
workOns.cameWith: It often drags other habits in with it. Not today — on every swing, your head stays level going back, your hips turn in place going back and your hips hold their height going back.

causes.lead: We checked every cause we know of for this one, and each was fine — so it may come from something we can't yet put a name to. Worth talking through with your coach.

rows.title: Ruled out — measured, and fine
items: You squat too much at address

drills.label: Trail hip load and hold
drills.instruction: Take your address position, make a slow backswing turn, and stop at the top. Feel the pressure in the trail hip socket rather than on the outside of the trail foot. Hold for three seconds, then return.
drills.targets: To feel the trail hip accepting the turn instead of the pelvis sliding away from the target.
drills.note: The stick is a feedback aid, not the drill. If the hip cannot rotate internally, the slide is the body finding the only route it has.
drills.equipment: an alignment stick outside the trail hip, optional

workOns.cue: As you turn back, feel your trail knee stay soft and pointing at the ball while your trail pocket turns behind you.
workOns.check: Film from down the line. At the top, your trail knee should look about as bent as it did at address.
workOns.target: Trail-knee bend lost by the top: less than 12°, on most swings. Today: 22°.
workOns.figureLabel: Each dot is one swing: trail-knee bend lost by the top, in degrees.

workOns.coachTerm: Coaches call the habit Trail knee straightens, or “standing up on it going back”.

steps.head: Rehearse without a ball
steps.body: Slow swings, ten at a time, feeling the change. This is where the new move is learned.

steps.head: Small swings with a ball
steps.body: Half swings at half speed. Keep the feel; ignore where the ball goes.

steps.head: Mix it in
steps.body: Full swings: one with the feel, then two normal ones. Film every fifth swing.

steps.head: One thing at a time
steps.body: Stay with work-on 1 until your next session. The rest of the list waits.

numbers.note: Path, face and offline: positive is right of target, negative left (right-handed golfer). Habits: how many of your work-ons showed on that swing. Typical: the middle value of your ten swings.

about.dates: This report covers your session on Tuesday 20 October 2026 and was prepared on 20 October 2026. If a session is re-analysed, the report is prepared again and carries the new date.
about.measured: 10 swings with a 7 iron, filmed down-the-line and face-on at high frame rate, with every ball measured by a GC Quad. Your body positions are read from the video by pose tracking; the club and ball numbers come from the launch monitor.
about.ranges: Each habit is judged against a target range. Most ranges are coaching judgement, set from what good ball-strikers do; a few come from published measurements. They are not fitted to you. A swing outside the range is not a mistake in itself — it is where the evidence points.
about.notChecked: Some things could not be checked on every swing: pelvis peak a spike (10 of 10); chest peak out of sight (10 of 10); club peak drawn, not judged (10 of 10). Nothing in this report depends on them.
